legal_003:n1.prompt:
You are helping me complete step legal_003:n1 of our IP assignment compliance process: 'List all team members' who need signed IP assignment (PIIA) agreements.

Goal: Produce a complete, accurate roster of every founder and employee (past and present, if still relevant) who should have signed a PIIA, pulled from our payroll system, {{vendor}}.

Before starting, ask me for anything you need, such as: confirmation that you have configured credentials to access {{vendor}}, whether to include contractors or only W-2/full-time employees, and whether to include terminated employees who worked during a relevant period.

Actions to take:
1. Using your configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}} and retrieve the current list of team members/employees, including full name, work email, employment status (active/terminated), start date, and role/title if available.
2. Organize this into a clean table or structured list, sorted by employment status (active first) and then alphabetically by last name.
3. Flag any records with missing or ambiguous data (e.g., no email, unclear status) so I can clarify.
4. Note any employees who appear to be founders (based on title, e.g., CEO, CTO, Founder) so they can be tracked separately if needed, since founders sometimes require a slightly different agreement flow.

What done looks like: A single, deduplicated list of all team members from {{vendor}} with name, email, status, and start date, ready to be cross-referenced against signed PIIA records in a later step.

Report back: Share the full roster (as a table), the total count of active and terminated members, and a short list of any data quality issues or ambiguous records you found that need my input before we proceed to checking signature status.

legal_003:n2.prompt:
You are helping me generate a signed-ready Proprietary Information and Inventions Assignment (PIIA) agreement for every founder and employee at my company. Before starting, ask me for anything you don't already have: (1) my legal company name and state/country of incorporation, (2) the full list of founders and employees who need a PIIA, with each person's full legal name, role/title, and start date, (3) the governing law/jurisdiction to use, and (4) whether I already have an approved PIIA template (and where it's stored, e.g., Google Drive, Notion, or a shared folder) or whether you should draft one from a standard, commonly-used PIIA template structure covering: assignment of inventions, confidentiality obligations, prior inventions disclosure schedule, and return of company property.

Once you have this information, do the following: pull or draft the base template, then create one individualized copy per person with their name, role, start date, and company details correctly merged in. Save each person's draft as a separate document named clearly (e.g., "PIIA_[FullName]_[Company].docx" or in your document tool of choice), and keep them organized in one folder or list. Flag any missing prior-inventions disclosures you need me to fill in.

Do not send these documents for signature and do not mark anyone as signed — this step is only about generating accurate, ready-to-review drafts. Legal review and execution remains a human step.

When finished, report back with: the total number of PIIAs generated, the file names/locations of each draft, any people missing required information, and a note confirming the drafts are ready for legal/founder review before signature.

legal_003:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for legal review of our Proprietary Information and Inventions Assignment Agreement (PIIA) template before we roll it out for founder/employee signatures. This review must ultimately be confirmed by a qualified attorney for enforceability in our jurisdiction — you cannot approve or sign off on this yourself.

First, ask me for anything you need that's missing: our company name/entity type, state or country of incorporation (and any other jurisdictions where employees work), whether we already have a draft PIIA template (and its location/file) or need to source a standard template, and the attorney or law firm we plan to use for review (name, email, or firm portal if we have one).

Then do the following:
1. Locate or draft a clean, organized PIIA template document, noting any placeholder fields (company name, employee name, effective date, governing law) that need to be filled in per jurisdiction.
2. Prepare a concise summary of open questions for the attorney: does it need California-compliant carve-outs, prior inventions exclusions, or multi-state variations; are there any employees in jurisdictions with special IP assignment rules.
3. Draft a short email or message to the attorney/firm requesting formal legal review and confirmation of enforceability, attaching or linking the template and the summary of questions.
4. Set up a simple tracking note (e.g., in a doc or task list) recording that the review request was sent, the date, and a placeholder for the attorney's response, since this is an async step — you'll need to check back later for their reply rather than assuming approval.

Do not mark the template as approved, finalized, or ready to use — that determination must come from the attorney. Once everything is drafted and the request is ready to send, stop for human sign-off so I can review and personally send it to the attorney.

legal_003:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare to send Proprietary Information and Invention Assignment Agreements (PIIAs) to all founders and employees using {{vendor}}, our legal-ops e-signature platform. 

First, ask me for anything you don't already have: (1) my company domain, (2) the current PIIA template/document to use, (3) a full list of founders and employees who need to sign, with their names and email addresses, and (4) confirmation that {{vendor}} is connected with configured credentials. 

Once you have these, do the following:
1. Draft the recipient/signer list, matching each person to the correct signing role in {{vendor}}.
2. Populate the PIIA template with each recipient's details (name, email, start date if relevant) as required by {{vendor}}'s document generation flow.
3. Prepare the bulk signature workflow in {{vendor}} — using its documented API, MCP server, or dashboard bulk-send feature — so that all PIIAs are queued and ready to be launched with proper routing to each signer.
4. Compile a checklist showing: total recipients, document version used, any missing emails or data, and the exact workflow/batch that will be triggered.

Do NOT actually launch or send the signature workflow yourself. Because a human must explicitly approve before this change is applied, you must stop for human sign-off after preparing the draft, populated documents, and checklist. Present everything to me for review and approval before any PIIAs are sent.

When done, report back with: the full recipient list and roles, confirmation the PIIA template was correctly populated for each person, the prepared workflow/batch identifier or name in {{vendor}}, and a clear note that the bulk send is staged and awaiting my explicit approval to launch.

legal_003:n5.prompt:
You are helping me track and follow up on unsigned IP assignment agreements (PIIAs) for founders and employees using {{vendor}}, our legal-ops e-signature platform. This is an async step: results (signature completions) will land over time, so you must poll for status rather than expect immediate completion.

First, ask me for anything you don't already have: (1) confirmation that you have access to {{vendor}} via my configured credentials, (2) the list of founders/employees who should have signed PIIAs, and (3) any deadline or target date for full completion.

Then, using {{vendor}}'s dashboard or API:
1. Check the status of all pending PIIA envelopes/signature requests and identify which recipients have not yet signed.
2. For each unsigned envelope, confirm the signing order and reminder settings are configured — if {{vendor}} supports automatic reminders and expirations on outstanding requests, ensure these are enabled so nudges go out without manual intervention.
3. Draft a short, polite follow-up message for each outstanding signer (email or in-app message) requesting they complete signing, referencing the PIIA and any deadline.
4. Set up or confirm a recurring check (e.g., via {{vendor}}'s renewal/deadline tracking or alerts) so you can monitor progress and flag any envelope that lapses or expires without being signed.
5. Log the current status of every recipient (signed / pending / expired) in a simple summary.

Done looks like: every founder/employee has a clear status, reminders are active on all pending envelopes, and you have a monitoring mechanism in place to catch new completions or lapses.

Report back to me with: the full status list, which reminders/drafts you prepared, and confirmation that polling/monitoring is active so you can flag me when all signatures are complete or when any envelope needs escalation.

legal_003:n6.prompt:
You are helping me file executed IP assignment agreements (PIIAs) into our {{vendor}} cloud storage account so we have a clean, auditable record for every founder and employee. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the list of employees/founders and the file names or file paths of their signed executed PIIA copies (assume they're on my local machine or a location I'll specify), and (2) my preferred folder structure/name if I have one (e.g., 'Legal/IP Assignments').

Using my configured credentials for {{vendor}}, do the following:
1. Create (or confirm existing) a dedicated folder for IP assignment records, structured as a lightweight data room — e.g., a parent 'Legal' folder with a subfolder for signed PIIAs.
2. Upload each signed executed PIIA file into that folder via {{vendor}}'s API (use resumable/session upload for larger files, direct upload for small ones).
3. For each uploaded file, set custom metadata/properties (employee name, document type = 'PIIA', date signed, status = 'executed') if the platform supports a metadata schema, so files are queryable later.
4. Confirm version history is enabled/retained for these files per {{vendor}}'s documented retention window, in case a corrected copy is later uploaded.
5. Generate a view-only shared link (or note access permissions) for the folder so it can be shared with counsel or investors during diligence, but do not change sharing settings beyond view-only/download-restricted unless I specify otherwise.

Done looks like: every signed PIIA is uploaded to the correct folder, tagged with metadata, and the folder has a view-only access link ready to share. Report back with: the folder location/link, a list of files uploaded with their metadata tags, and confirmation that version history is active. Flag any files that failed to upload or lacked a signature so I can follow up.
